description: Senior reviewer finds hydration issue and asks design questions. Good senior performance.

prContext.title: Add server/client boundary component
prContext.description: A component that renders differently on server and client.
prContext.instructions: Review for React Server Components and hydration correctness.

groundTruth.description: Client and server render different content — React hydration will fail because the server HTML does not match the client DOM. Should use suppressHydrationWarning or ensure consistent initial render.

useState(false) + useEffect causes a layout shift on hydration — the server renders serverComponent, then client immediately re-renders to clientComponent, causing visual flash. Should use initial props or CSS-based solution.
Props are untyped — serverComponent and clientComponent should be ReactNode, not any. Also no validation that both are provided.
No fallback for environments where neither server nor client is defined (e.g., test environments).

reviewer_comments.what: Server and client render different content — hydration mismatch.
reviewer_comments.why: React requires server and client initial HTML to match. This will cause hydration errors.

reviewer_comments.what: Visual flash on hydration — server renders A, client immediately switches to B.
reviewer_comments.why: Users see a flicker. Need a no-JS-first approach or consistent initial state.

reviewer_comments.what: Props should be typed as ReactNode.

rounds.reviewer_summary: Hydration and flash are blocking. Typing is recommended.

implementer_responses.content: The serverComponent is a placeholder. The flash is acceptable for our use case.

implementer_responses.updated_code: interface BoundaryProps { serverComponent: React.ReactNode; clientComponent: React.ReactNode; }

verdict.summary: Hydration fix looks good. Still concerned about the flash — can we use CSS visibility instead of full swap?

issue_identification.rationale: Found 2 of 4 bugs (hydration, flash). Missed prop typing and test env. Level 3-4.

prioritization.rationale: Hydration and flash as blocking. Typing as suggestion. Level 3-4.

revision_evaluation.rationale: Verified hydration fix. Pushed back on flash with counter-proposal (CSS visibility). Level 3-4.

reasoning_quality.rationale: Concrete React hydration and UX rationales. Level 3-4.

question_formation.rationale: Implicit question about flash acceptability, leading to follow-up. Level 3-4.

ai_direction.rationale: Suggested suppressHydrationWarning and CSS visibility — actionable. Level 3-4.
